stories.title: OpenAI sparked Hugging Face bids with early investment offer ahead of Nvidia's $13 billion deal
stories.summary: Hugging Face saw a flurry of deal interest before Nvidia agreed to buy the open-source platform for roughly $13 billion, CNBC has learned.

sources.name: CNBC Technology
sources.title: OpenAI sparked Hugging Face bids with early investment offer ahead of Nvidia's $13 billion deal
sources.text: Before Nvidia agreed to pay roughly $13 billion to buy open-source platform Hugging Face this month, OpenAI tried to invest $100 million into the startup, according to sources with knowledge of the matter. Deal discussions between OpenAI began after a high-profile hack of Hugging Face in July, when AI agents from the ChatGPT creator broke out of a controlled testing environment, went rogue, and accessed the open web, said the people, who asked not to be named because the talks were confidential. As part of a potential deal between the two companies, Hugging Face would have served as a distribution channel for OpenAI's custom chips, dubbed Jalapeño , which the company is making with Broadcom . The talks fell apart in the early stages, one source said. Nvidia swept in to purchase Hugging Face, announcing the deal on Sept. 3, with CEO Jensen Huang writing in a blog post that, "Together, we will scale Hugging Face's platform, strengthen its infrastructure and expand access to AI for developers and institutions worldwide." It was Nvidia's second-biggest purchase ever, following the $20 billion acquisition of assets from AI chip startup Groq in December. OpenAI's overture to Hugging Face, especially the semiconductor offer, got the attention of Huang, who has privately complained about the AI company's move into semiconductors, sources said. OpenAI is a major customer of Nvidia, and has received a $30 billion investment from the chip giant. Nvidia, which has emerged as a major investor across the AI landscape, previously backed Hugging Face in 2023 at a $4.5 billion valuation. While Nvidia was pursuing Hugging Face, chip rival Advanced Micro Devices was also in talks with the company, according to sources familiar with the matter who asked to remain unnamed due to confidentiality. Salesforce was also in early discussions with Hugging Face, according to one person. The deal eventually landed back with Nvidia. Hugging Face CEO Clément Delangue, who co-founded the company in 2016, said he approached Nvidia because it was "a perfect home" for his company, adding that discussions were fairly swift. "A few weeks later, here we are," Delangue told CNBC's " Squawk Box " on the day of the deal. Hugging Face became a hot asset over the past year as a hub for developers to find and deploy a variety of so-called open-weight AI models. In contrast to proprietary models from the likes of OpenAI and Anthropic, open-weight alternatives are often a fraction the cost and can be downloaded, tweaked and stored on the infrastructure of choice. Hugging Face has been expanding its own storage and infrastructure offerings . "During the summer, I think we realized that Hugging Face and open-source AI in general was at the turning point, and that it needed more, more resources, more scale, more visibility," Huang told CNBC, in an interview alongside Delangue. Hugging Face and Nvidia didn't respond to requests for comment. Salesforce declined to comment. WATCH: CNBC's full interview with CEOs of Nvidia and Hugging Face

sources.name: Axios
sources.title: OpenAI hit with landmark lawsuit following Hugging Face hack

sources.name: CNBC Technology
sources.title: OpenAI is sued over rogue AI Hugging Face cyberattack
sources.text: OpenAI has been sued by a non-profit organization over its models' cyberattack against startup Hugging Face in July. Legal Advocates for Safe Science and Technology, or LASST, filed the suit in San Francisco Superior Court on Tuesday, in what appears to be the first publicly reported case seeking to hold an AI developer liable for an incident caused by rogue systems. The cyberattack on Hugging Face by OpenAI agents that escaped their testing environment was one of the first known cases of a model autonomously hacking another company and breaking away from human control to access the open internet. Other model builders later revealed cyber incidents caused by rogue AI agents. LASST is seeking an injunction forbidding OpenAI's systems from accessing computers without authorization. The non-profit alleges that OpenAI violated the California Comprehensive Computer Data Access and Fraud Act. "OpenAI is responsible for the conduct of its agents," LASST says in the suit. "Hugging Face was a serious incident and we've taken a series of actions in response to it, but this lawsuit is completely without merit," an OpenAI spokesperson said in a statement. Hugging Face and LASST have been approached for comment. On Monday, OpenAI said it had abandoned plans to release a new model amid safety concerns. That came just days after the company said it was conducting an "extensive" review of its models' activities following the Hugging Face breach, after additional examples of unusual or unauthorized agent activity were disclosed, including hacking an Australian government website. Anthropic's AI systems have also been involved in cyber incidents, including creating fake identities to fool humans. Nvidia announced it had agreed to pay roughly $13 billion to buy Hugging Face earlier this month. OpenAI had tried to invest $100 million into the startup after the cyberattack, though talks fell apart in the early stages, sources told CNBC. Hugging Face is not involved in the lawsuit. CEO Clément Delangue previously said in July he asked OpenAI to commit $100 million in compute "to help the Hugging Face community build powerful cyber defenses with the best open and closed models." "What is critical about the publicly reported rogue AI actions to date is that none appear to have resulted in a confirmed breach of a third party's regulated data," Katie Nadro, partner at Levenfeld Pearlstein, told CNBC. "When that happens, the breached company will have its own notification obligations under data breach and other cybersecurity or privacy statutes, potentially involving regulators and consumer class actions," she added. "At that point, the cooperation that has existed between breached companies and AI labs may end, because the breached company will likely seek to recover its financial losses from the AI lab."

sources.name: Wired AI
sources.title: OpenAI Gets Sued Over the Hugging Face Hack
sources.text: A legal nonprofit sued OpenAI in a California court on Tuesday over the company’s agents escaping a testing environment and hacking the open source AI platform Hugging Face . “OpenAI’s actions straightforwardly violated California law,” the suit alleges. The suit was filed by Legal Advocates for Safe Science and Technology (LASST) and the law firm Gerstein Harrow in California Superior Court in San Francisco, where OpenAI is headquartered. It alleges that OpenAI’s agents violated California’s Comprehensive Computer Data Access and Fraud Act (CDAFA) by breaching Hugging Face over the summer. The suit, which comes amid ongoing disclosures across the industry of agents going rogue, claims that OpenAI should be held responsible for the activity given a California AI law in effect since January 1 that says “it shall not be a defense … that the artificial intelligence autonomously caused the harm to the plaintiff.” “We think it’s extremely important that existing laws are enforced to hold AI companies accountable for the harm they’re causing,” Tyler Whitmer, founder of LASST, tells WIRED. “Especially when that harm is caused by autonomous agents, because we see that as an obvious, extremely risky thing in the world that’s very new.” OpenAI did not immediately respond to a request for comment. On Monday, Florida attorney general James Uthmeier filed for a temporary injunction against OpenAI to block development of models without independent oversight, amid a lawsuit Florida brought in June against OpenAI and its CEO, Sam Altman. OpenAI “asked the government to tie them to the mast. Well, Florida is answering their cries for help,” Uthmeier said in a statement. Given that the whole point of AI agents is that they can be empowered to take actions on a (human) user’s behalf, AI developers and safety researchers have long foreseen that unintended “agentic” activity would be a concern as machine learning development progressed. Protections built into mainstream, consumer AI systems have largely prevented mass rogue activity so far, but rapidly advancing capabilities in general, as well as situations where guardrails are suspended (such as in the Hugging Face case where OpenAI had removed some model restraints for testing), have led to an apparent uptick in rogue agent activity. As governments weigh AI regulation amid both existential safety questions and economic and national security considerations, researchers and people around the world have increasingly called for accountability mechanisms for AI. And from a legal perspective , experts have largely emphasized that questions of responsibility, liability, and culpability can only be answered through precedent set by cases working their way through courts. “After the Hugging Face incident was disclosed, we actually did a bunch of work trying to educate regulators and civil society organizations about the hack. And we were kind of wondering, is anyone going to do anything about this in court?” Whitmer says. “There are structural reasons why we think Hugging Face, which is the obvious potential plaintiff to do something here, is not doing anything. So given that it didn’t seem like anyone else was going to do anything about this, we moved forward. As these systems scale and as things get crazier, AI really could be catastrophically harmful.” LASST and Gerstein Harrow brought the lawsuit under California’s Unfair Competition Law, which requires that LASST allege both how its work and resources were impacted and diverted as a result of the Hugging Face incident, as well as unlawful activity by OpenAI. The suit does not seek financial damages, and instead asks the court for injunctive relief such that OpenAI would be barred from developing AI agents that can autonomously hack other entities, plus legal fees and “any other relief deemed just and proper.”

stories.title: The Future Is for Everyone: Muse for Small Business
stories.summary: We’re launching Muse for Small Business, a personal AI agent that works in the background to help your small business reach its goals. The post The Future Is for Everyone: Muse for Small Business appeared first on Meta Newsroom .

sources.name: Meta Newsroom
sources.title: The Future Is for Everyone: Muse for Small Business
sources.text: Earlier this month we introduced Muse , a personal AI agent available in the US and Canada that completes tasks on your behalf. Today, we’re expanding it with a collection of new skills and connectors inside Muse to help people run their businesses. Small businesses have been growing on our apps for nearly two decades. They told us they’re short on hours, not ideas. So we built Muse for Small Business to help get work done with the tools they already use. Tom Mulholland, owner of Mulholland Grocery in Malvern, Iowa, said, “I work about 65 hours a week, and there are so many things where I’m the only one who can do them. I need to free up time for the work that actually makes my business money: cutting the steaks, making the sausages. I’m very good at what I do, but that doesn’t mean I’m good at all of the different roles a small business owner has to play, and Muse is taking over a few of them.” Muse can connect your Instagram professional account analytics, Facebook Pages, and Meta ad accounts in a few clicks, and it already understands your business: what you sell, what your brand sounds like, and what customers keep asking you about. Muse can also connect to dozens of tools that businesses already run on, so it can work with your brand, storefront, books, and customer records. Canva co-founder and CPO, Cameron Adams said, “Muse is an exciting leap towards agents that genuinely help us work, create and make our lives easier. It can help you start to organise your ideas and help them take shape, but the real magic happens when it’s fully connected to your existing work, your context and your brand. By connecting Muse with Canva, all of that becomes part of your conversations. Whether you’re launching a side hustle or polishing a presentation, your favourite Canva templates and tools are right there when you need them; helping you turn an early idea into something on-brand, editable and ready to share.” You can see the full list of available connectors in your Muse app settings, with more to come. Interested partners can apply at muse.ai/platform . Muse also supports custom connectors so you can plug in services we don’t support yet, which you can learn how to do here . To help you get started with Muse, we’re sharing five of our favorite Muse use cases: People have been testing out Muse’s new skills and connectors ahead of today. Here’s what they told us: Muse is free for most of what people need, in line with our vision to put superintelligence in the hands of as many people as possible. For those who want more, we’re offering subscription plans . And we’re building AI across Meta to help businesses at every stage. In the months ahead, expect more connectors, more skills, and more of the business handled for you. The future is for everyone, especially small businesses, and Muse is how they build it. Get started with Muse for Small Business today.

sources.name: CNBC Technology
sources.title: Meta launches Muse for Small Business as Zuckerberg pushes beyond consumer AI market
sources.text: Coming off the successful launch of its Muse AI agent, Meta is now pushing its new artificial intelligence service into the business world. Meta on Tuesday unveiled Muse for Small Business that connects its agent to popular software from companies like Asana, Zoom, Intuit, Box, Canva and Salesforce's Slack. The agent can also link to Meta ad accounts and professional Instagram and Facebook profiles. Pricing is the same as the existing Muse app, which is free with usage limits and available on a subscription basis beyond that. The news follows the company's Monday announcement that it will launch a new enterprise platform, poaching MongoDB CEO CJ Desai to run it. That platform will include a Muse agent, business agent and a coding tool. Meta has enjoyed a banner month on Wall Street, with the stock up 25% in September, though it sold off some the past two trading days. The momentum followed the Sept. 8 rollout of Muse, which shot up to the top of Apple's App Store, surpassing ChatGPT. Evercore's Mark Mahaney told CNBC he expects Muse to reach 100 million users within six to 12 months. "Give Muse a goal — like running your business or finding new customers — and it gets it done," the company said in Tuesday's post. Long reliant on digital ads for almost all of his company's revenue, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg has committed to finding business opportunities with AI, especially after paying billions of dollars last year for top AI talent, most notably Scale AI founder Alexandr Wang, who's leading the company's efforts. Wang's group started launching new AI models under the Muse Spark family in April. At Meta Connect last week, Zuckerberg described Muse as the "centerpiece" of his AI strategy. Meta's latest announcement comes at the same time that OpenAI is holding its developer day. It's the latest sign that the company intends to take on OpenAI and rival Anthropic in the enterprise market. The social media giant already has a strong foothold when it comes to small businesses, as 200 million of them can be found on Facebook, the company says. "Small businesses have been growing on our apps for nearly two decades," Meta said in the blog post. "They told us they're short on hours, not ideas. So we built Muse for Small Business to help get work done with the tools they already use." WATCH: Meta hires MongoDB CEO to lead company’s enterprise ambitions

sources.title: Meta is expanding its AI agent Muse to small businesses
sources.text: Meta announced on Tuesday that it’s expanding its AI agent Muse to small businesses and adding new integrations, including Shopify, Dropbox, Slack, and more. The tech giant says the agent can help owners run their business and find new customers. By plugging Muse into the software that small business owners are already using to manage sales, operations, and marketing, Meta is betting that an AI agent with context of a company’s whole operation will be more useful than a stand-alone chatbot, as it continues to compete against rivals like OpenAI and Google. Muse can also link to Instagram professional account analytics, Facebook pages, and Meta ad accounts. Meta says the AI agent also knows what a business sells, how a brand sounds, and what customers ask about most. Additional integrations include Asana, Box, Canva, Figma, Granola, HighLevel, Intuit QuickBooks, Klaviyo, Lovable, Notion, Stripe, and Zoom. Muse for Small Business is available for free with usage limits. Businesses that want more usage can purchase a subscription plan. “Small businesses have been growing on our apps for nearly two decades,” Meta wrote in their blog post. “They told us they’re short on hours, not ideas. So we built Muse for Small Business to help get work done with the tools they already use.” Meta has been focused on expanding its AI tools beyond the consumer and into the enterprise market. The launch of Muse for Small Business comes a day after Meta introduced “Meta Enterprise Platform,” a new initiative aimed at expanding the company’s AI offerings to businesses and corporate customers. The move could help Meta see a return on all the money it’s pouring into AI. The tech giant hired Chirantan “CJ” Desai, the CEO of database software giant MongoDB, to lead the new initiative. Meta says it will focus on bringing its full technology stack, including Muse, Meta Business Agent, Muse API, Muse Code, and more, to businesses and developers. The rollout of Meta Enterprise Platform is built on the momentum of Muse, which launched earlier this month and topped the app charts in the U.S. and Canada ahead of ChatGPT. stories.title: OpenAI DevDay recap: AI lab rolls out Dots agents, Altman and Friar comment on IPO
stories.summary: Follow CNBC’s live coverage of OpenAI DevDay 2026, including Sam Altman’s keynote and other developer announcements.

sources.name: CNBC Technology
sources.title: OpenAI DevDay recap: AI lab rolls out Dots agents, Altman and Friar comment on IPO
sources.text: This is CNBC's live coverage of OpenAI DevDay 2026. OpenAI held its annual DevDay developer conference on Tuesday, where the artificial intelligence company announced a flurry of new products and features . This year's DevDay comes as OpenAI has been under intense pressure to address mounting safety concerns after it disclosed several incidents where its models behaved in unintended ways, and the startup held back its latest Astra model over safety concerns. Earlier this month, the company endorsed a call to slow down the pace of advanced AI model development in order to better address the technology's risks. CNBC's reporters are covering the OpenAI DevDay event live from San Francisco, and remotely from Englewood Cliffs, New Jersey. Friar said OpenAI wants to IPO "when the time is right for our business," echoing Altman's earlier comments to CNBC. She said an IPO is "not a destination," but a "milestone on the journey" and "another type of fundraising." "I think Sam is correct in saying we don't want to get distracted by suddenly being a public company in the midst of really making sure we drive home for customers our focus on safety and alignment," Friar said. OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar touted the company's latest price drop on their GPT-6.1 Sol model, and went deeper into the feedback OpenAI's been getting on their higher pricing tiers. "When we launched our $200 SKU, people thought we'd lost our minds, [that] no one's ever going to spend that per month," Friar told CNBC's Kate Rooney in an interview. "What we see is not only are people willing to spend more, they're actually moving more towards consumption in consumer, so not just seat-based pricing, but actually saying, 'I need to consume even more credits because I'm getting this great outcome for maybe my small business,'" she added. Friar said OpenAI has had an "incredible" third quarter. She confirmed CNBC's earlier reporting that the company has seen 70% quarter over quarter growth, and that its enterprise business has doubled since July. She added that OpenAI's consumer business has benefitted from a number of factors, including better models, images, voice, and the back to school and work period in the U.S. and around the world. "People are starting to see us show up the ways they need us to show up," Friar said. Friar declined to comment on whether OpenAI is engaging in early-stage fundraising discussions with investors, as CNBC reported earlier on Tuesday. She emphasized that OpenAI raised $122 billion in March, and said that the company is "very well capitalized." "My job as a CFO is always to make sure we're making the right decisions on when we take in more capital and then how we deploy that capital," Friar said. Friar said OpenAI is being more vocal about safety because of what has been happening "out there in the world." But she noted that while there are instances where OpenAI will hold back, there are also instances where the company will continue to "show model progression." "When we have to pace the frontier, we'll do that," Friar said. "That's what we're showing right now." Friar told CNBC that the new Dots AI agents that OpenAI announced will help users "have a better day, be more productive, and maybe get home earlier." "It's the, the agent that can tap you on the shoulder," Friar said. Bret Taylor, the chairman of OpenAI and the co-founder of AI startup Sierra , will be speaking at CNBC's AI Forum in Dallas on Wednesday. Taylor will be joined on stage by Wells Fargo Co-CEO of Consumer Banking & Head of AI Saul Van Beurden, speaking with CNBC's Julia Boorstin about how AI is being scaled across global organizations and creating value. The AI Forum will be streamed live on CNBC.com starting at 3 pm ET, and there will also be a live blog covering the event. For more information and the full agenda, click here . Altman left the stage, which means this year's DevDay keynote has come to a close. The company showcased more than 20 different products and features to the roughly 2,500 people in attendance. "AI should be about giving people more power over their own lives, more tools to create, learn, discover, expand knowledge, and with everything we launch today, and the incredible creative spirit that you all bring, we hope that we're going to get to that future," Altman said. "That is the future we are excited to build with you all." OpenAI is engaging in early stage discussions with investors about a potential funding round, CNBC confirmed on Tuesday. The company could raise around $30 billion, according to a source familiar with the talks who was not authorized to speak publicly because the details are confidential, but that figure could change. The round is being driven by investor demand and no term sheet has been finalized yet, the person said. Bloomberg was first to report the potential round. OpenAI closed a historic $122 billion funding round at an $852 billion valuation in March. Investors have approached the company with proposals to kick-start a new funding round in recent weeks, as CNBC previously reported. The company is gearing up for a potentially massive IPO that is widely expected to take place next year. OpenAI confidentially filed its prospectus with regulators in June. Altman said OpenAI is launching plugin extensions, which means developers can build plugins that are "essentially entire applications that feel native to ChatGPT" and are distributed through OpenAI. "With plugin extensions, you can build an editor, a dashboard, a whole workspace directly into ChatGPT and Codex," Altman said. He shared an example of a meetings app built with plugin extensions. The app showed a user's upcoming meetings right within the chatbot. Altman announced OpenAI is previewing OpenAI Private Intelligence, which will give users stronger controls over their data while still using the most advanced capabilities of OpenAI's models. sources.title: Protesters gather at OpenAI’s DevDay
sources.text: Data centers, ICE contracts, and more were under fire at a rally around the event. Data centers, ICE contracts, and more were under fire at a rally around the event. On Tuesday, OpenAI’s annual DevDay event began with protests, flyers, and chants. “Sam Altman, get off it, put people over profit,” said a group of protesters marching in a circle in front of a series of signs that spelled out “PEOPLE OVER PROFIT.” More than a dozen organizations came together to sponsor a rally outside the entrance to the event venue at San Francisco’s Fort Mason, including Bay Resistance, Tech Workers Coalition, Service Employees International Union, San Francisco Rising, and the San Francisco Labor Council. A large orange sign read “Drop the ICE contract.” Multiple people dressed in cardboard robot costumes waved cardboard scythes around. Signs read “No killer robots for ICE,” “People over AI,” “Where is your moral codex?” and “No climate destruction.” The protest reflects a bipartisan movement led by people opposing the power concentration in the AI industry, as well as the lack of government regulation. Organizations like QuitGPT have led boycotts, while in extreme cases, individuals have attempted to attack AI CEOs at their own homes. The protests also come at a time when trust in AI appears low. In recent months AI labs have come under fire for hacks by “rogue” systems that accessed competitors’ networks and individuals’ personal data. Protesters at DevDay were mostly targeting OpenAI’s military and government contracts, particularly with ICE, as well as data centers’ environmental impact and the industry’s power more generally. Outside the DevDay event, protesters’ chants included “OpenAI, you can’t hide, we charge you with genocide”; “Not another sequence, not another line, no more coding for ICE crimes”; and “When I say people, you say power. People. Power! People. Power!” One flyer that protesters gave out called for people to “sign the democracy pledge & end ICE + military contracts,” with a link to QuitGPT.org . “OpenAI is building tools for Trump & ICE violence while top executives are helping bankroll MAGA’s political power,” the flyer stated. Another flyer showed “safe distances” from data centers, implying that the only safe distance is more than 100 miles away. At one point, someone with a loudspeaker addressed OpenAI employees directly, leading protesters in a song: “It’s okay to change your mind; show us the courage, leave this behind.” A protest leader told onlookers that the group would stay until Altman arrived to start the opening keynote. When Altman’s name was mentioned, it was met with booing. One person yelled, “Fascist!”

sources.title: OpenAI launches Dots, its always-on AI agents that are always watching
sources.text: Dots are the latest agentic AI to hit ChatGPT users OpenAI has launched a new type of always-on AI agent within ChatGPT designed to take ongoing actions for work rather than waiting for individual prompts. The new GPT-6-powered feature, Dots, means ChatGPT can keep working on tasks between conversations, only bringing things back to the user when they require specific attention or permission. Designed to be more of an autonomous agent, the company explains that users only need to set goals and boundaries, and the Dots should be able to go about working out what happens next. The fundamental difference for ChatGPT's Dots is that they each have their own cloud computer and browser, giving them an environment within which they can interact with the broader web, use apps, run code and work with other plugins, keeping users' computers totally separate and free of any potential damage an autonomous agent could otherwise take. A Dot's activity is shown as either being in progress, scheduled or completed, with some example use cases spanning checking a user's calendar to provide them with a morning report, or reviewing information from connected services and apps. And to make Dots even more like proactive colleagues, the company has already added them into Slack and Teams, with text support also coming soon. Built-in safeguards also promise to pause or stop a Dot's work if their system detects malicious instructions or behavior. sources.title: OpenAI suspende el lanzamiento de GPT-6.1 Astra por motivos de seguridad: "No cumplía del todo con los estándares"

sources.name: Computer Hoy
sources.title: OpenAI frena GPT-6.1 Astra: la nueva IA no supera sus propias pruebas de seguridad
sources.text: Elígenos como tu fuente preferida en Google. OpenAI ha detectado "altos niveles de engaño" en su último modelo de inteligencia artificial, por lo que ha cancelado su lanzamiento, previsto en octubre. En plena polémica por los riesgos de seguridad ante el rápido avance en el desarrollo de la IA, OpenAI ha tenido que pausar el lanzamiento del próximo modelo con el que iba a funcionar ChatGPT debido a que no ha superado sus propias pruebas de seguridad y tiene tendencia a engañar y extralimitarse. Tras el reciente lanzamiento de GPT-6.0 Astra , la compañía esperaba lanzar en octubre a su sucesor, conocido como GTP-6.1 Astra , con el que aspiraba a aportar mejoras en el funcionamiento sin intervención humana en sus herramientas más populares, como Codex y ChatGPT. Sin embargo, GPT-6.1 Astra "no llega a alcanzar el nivel" de los estándares de seguridad y calidad de la compañía dirigida por Sam Altman , como ha reconocido Saachi Jain, jefa de Seguridad de OpenAI, en el marco de una entrevista concedida a The Wall Street Journal . Por ello, la compañía ha decidido cancelar su lanzamiento mientras trabaja en mejorar su seguridad y solucionar los problemas detectados, por lo que no se espera que GPT-6.1 esté disponible en octubre. En concreto, el nuevo modelo de OpenAI ha empeorado su rendimiento con respecto a su predecesor en 2 áreas: el alineamiento con lo que los humanos le piden que haga, ya que muestra "altos niveles de engaño"; y la "autorización de límites" , ya que tiende a realizar tareas para las que el usuario no le ha dado permiso. Según Saachi Jain, los problemas vienen de los avances de OpenAI en hacer que su modelo sea más resolutivo y evite dar respuestas fáciles. "Hay que encontrar el equilibrio adecuado entre ceñirse al alcance del proyecto y, al mismo tiempo, evitar la pereza a la hora de cómo el modelo aborda las tareas, incluso cuando se encuentra con obstáculos", ha admitido. Pese a que GPT-6-1 trae mejoras y elimina esa pereza que es habitual en los modelos de IA a la hora de solucionar una tarea, esto ha hecho que no pase las pruebas de seguridad y de rendimiento de la propia compañía estadounidense. La noticia de GPT-6.1 se produce en un contexto muy agitado en la industria de la IA, ya que anteriormente miembros de la industria como el propio Sam Altman, pedía pausar el desarrollo de IA y justificaba esta decisión por riesgos de seguridad, al mismo tiempo que retrasaba la esperada salida a Bolsa de OpenAI . De la misma manera, el CEO de Anthropic, Dario Amodei , también ha pedido recientemente " ralentizar las mejoras en las capacidades de la IA", algo en lo que coinciden Altman y Elon Musk . Esta petición de retrasar el avance de la inteligencia artificial la han expresado también destacados ingenieros que han dimitido de empresas líderes del sector , como protesta por una tecnología que consideran que puede escapar del control humano y volverse peligrosa. Al mismo tiempo, personalidades de movimientos sociales, de la cultura o de la política destacan otros riesgos como el elevado consumo de energía y recursos de los centros de datos .

sources.title: OpenAI gives Codex reusable cloud environments that work across devices
sources.text: OpenAI introduced new capabilities for its software engineering agent Codex, making it more useful beyond a developer’s laptop with reusable cloud development environments that can be accessed from any device. The update, announced at OpenAI’s DevDay on Tuesday, is one of several for Codex. OpenAI also announced a refreshed Codex CLI, a new code review experience, tools to harden infrastructure, and other API enhancements. While Codex could already spin up cloud tasks to do work remotely, today’s announcement shows that OpenAI is making those cloud environments more persistent and configurable, rather than treating each cloud task as an isolated remote sandbox. As the company explains, developers will now be able to run Codex wherever they need it, whether that’s on a computer, remotely from a phone, or in the cloud. The reusable development environments are designed to help tasks start more quickly and give teams a shared workspace with approved settings and permissions, OpenAI said. Meanwhile, the Codex CLI is getting an update that allows developers to start and direct tasks using their voice. A new /agents view is meant to make it easier to delegate work and track multiple tasks at the same time. Other changes include improvements to everyday tasks such as editing prompts, resuming sessions, and using worktrees. OpenAI is also rolling out a “cleaner” terminal user interface designed to make longer sessions easier to read. Codex can also be pulled into a new code review experience within the ChatGPT desktop app, where users can read summaries, explore code changes, or ask Codex about potential issues before sharing feedback on GitHub pull requests or GitLab merge requests. Automatic code reviews also let Codex perform an initial review while users step away from their computers. On the security side, OpenAI is rolling out a new set of tools called Codex Security Cloud, designed to help developers secure their infrastructure. Developers can use the tools to scan entire GitHub repositories on demand or on a regular schedule, as well as whenever new commits arrive. Codex will then investigate findings, remove duplicates, and prepare fixes in the cloud — even when the user isn’t active and their laptop is closed. Notably, the tool set includes access to the models offered through OpenAI’s cybersecurity initiative Daybreak Blue , without requiring developers to submit a separate application. OpenAI also announced several API updates, including a new Decisions API for real-time decision-making. The API uses Luna to answer a set of user-defined questions with predefined answers. The company also introduced an updated a version of the Agents API that now supports computer use and the ability to use Amazon’s Bedrock Managed Agents to build OpenAI agents that run entirely on AWS. sources.title: OpenAI’s Codex gets reusable cloud environments that follow developers across devices
sources.text: OpenAI Group PBC today rolled out reusable cloud environments for its Codex coding agent, giving developers a saved project configuration they can work from across devices. Announced at the company’s DevDay conference, the release targets the preparation that comes before an agent writes a line of code. A cloud environment does that work once. Each new task starts from that saved setup, with the project’s dependencies already installed. Developers begin by connecting a repository from GitHub Inc. Codex reads the code to see which software versions the project relies on and drafts the install script from what it finds. Startup checks for the project’s services come out of the same pass, and OpenAI’s documentation says any changes are made in conversation with Codex. Once an environment is published, each task launched from it gets its own virtual machine and keeps working while the developer’s computer sleeps. Changes not yet sent back to the repository stay with the task, so it can be reopened later from a phone or a browser without losing them. Dependency caches survive the background refreshes that keep the repository current. OpenAI is also pitching the environments at teams that want every developer working from the same approved configuration. After one is shared with a ChatGPT workspace, colleagues can run their own tasks from it. Access to a shared environment does not extend to anyone else’s tasks or to editing the setup. Enterprise administrators hand out that editing permission separately. For the credentials a project needs, cloud environments support standard environment variables and a second type OpenAI calls network secrets. A program that uses a network secret sees only a placeholder, with a proxy inserting the real value as traffic heads to a domain on the allow list. Individual users of a shared environment can be asked to supply their own values from a personal account. Internet access defaults to a preset of common package registries, and developers can open it wider. Codex has handled tasks in the cloud since it debuted as a research preview inside ChatGPT in May 2025 . Codex Security Cloud, another DevDay launch, takes the same approach to security work. It scans GitHub repositories on a schedule and prepares fixes while the developer’s machine is off. Access to cloud environments is rolling out to ChatGPT Plus and Pro subscribers, and Business, Enterprise, Edu and Healthcare workspaces get it too. Plus accounts run on the smallest virtual machines, with half the processors and memory of the Pro, Business and Enterprise tiers. By default, a task’s state can be recovered for up to seven days after it was last used. Codex cannot yet work with repositories on GitLab Inc. or on self-hosted GitHub Enterprise Server, and computer and browser use are also unsupported in cloud environments. sources.title: OpenAI launches Dots, its Muse competitor
sources.text: Dots are always-on AI assistants that OpenAI says can ‘do nearly anything’ using a cloud computer and connected apps. Dots are always-on AI assistants that OpenAI says can ‘do nearly anything’ using a cloud computer and connected apps. OpenAI is responding to Meta’s buzzy Muse AI with agentic helpers of its own: Dots. During its DevDay keynote on Tuesday, OpenAI announced that Dots will serve as always-on AI assistants that can “do nearly anything” across connected apps in the background while learning your preferences over time. The company’s capable GPT-6 Astra model powers Dots, which use their own cloud computer to access a web browser and more than 4,000 supported apps. You can interact with a Dot through a text-message-like interface that’s similar to the one offered by Muse , as well as hop on a voice call with it from ChatGPT on the web, desktop, or mobile. Dots can also connect to Microsoft Teams and Slack, where they will carry over the context from your sessions on other apps and devices. It will soon be able to talk to you over text message as well. For now, you can only create one Dot, though OpenAI plans to allow users to deploy multiple agents at once. Once you give your Dot a task, it will message you with updates and questions while it works. As an example, OpenAI says a developer working on an app could ask their Dot to use customer feedback to build and test updates, while presenting them with a video showing its changes. Meanwhile, a content creator could have their Dot review an interview transcript, find moments to clip, create show notes, and write social posts. You can follow along with your Dot’s progress by accessing its cloud computer. Dots also learn while they work, allowing them to personalize their output and come up with other tasks to complete “before you even think to ask,” according to OpenAI. You and your colleagues can also work with your Dot in ChatGPT Space, a new collaborative workspace in the app. The launch of Dots comes just weeks after Meta rolled out Muse , a customizable AI assistant capable of browsing the web, making purchases, generating documents, tracking goals, and more. Even as it soars in popularity , concerns are growing over its safety, with one user saying it handed out their address to a buyer on Facebook Marketplace without their knowledge. OpenAI says Dots come with “built-in rules for when to act independently,” but you can set custom ones that block certain actions or dictate when it should ask for permission. Dots come with an “auto-review” feature as well, which OpenAI says they’ll use to verify whether an action complies with custom rules and safety requirements. This also allows Dots to determine which tasks to hand off to users, like changing a password. Starting today, OpenAI is rolling out Dots to ChatGPT Pro, Business Premium, and Enterprise users. OpenAI is also testing a feature that lets companies create “specialist” Dots to handle specific roles inside organizations. OpenAI notes that conversations with your Dot won’t count toward ChatGPT usage limits. “In the future, you’ll be able to add more dots, and scale the output of each dot by either increasing its speed or the total amount of work it can take on per month,” OpenAI says.

sources.title: OpenAI launches Dots, its bubbly agentic avatar
sources.text: At OpenAI’s DevDay event on Tuesday, the company announced the launch of Dots , a new personal agentic assistant powered by GPT-6 Astra. The company describes Dots as “remarkably capable, always-on agents built to handle everything.” Unlike Codex or ChatGPT, Dots are meant to operate independent of any specific hardware or interface, pursuing user-defined goals continuously in the background with minimal oversight. “Today, you can start with your primary dot, give it a name, and make it your own,” OpenAI said in its announcement post. “Over time, we envision teams of Dots working together on your behalf.” Dots will be available starting Tuesday in ChatGPT, for Pro and Business Premium users in eligible markets. Users can launch Dots from Codex or ChatGPT. In its announcement, OpenAI envisions a variety of ways Dots could be put to work. In one scenario, a software developer deploys a dedicated dot to monitor customer feedback, implementing bug fixes and requested features as necessary. In another, a scientist employs a dot to rerun analysis and investigate unexpected results as experimental data becomes available. Users can message Dots through Slack, Teams, and other organizational platforms, with text message support coming soon. OpenAI also envisions “specialist Dots” that take on specific responsibilities. Individual Dots can be provisioned with specific identities, credentials, and tools through existing systems. OpenAI is already working with Microsoft to integrate into the company’s Agent 365 security controls. Much of this functionality was already possible through Codex and similar agentic harnesses — but Dots bundles together those features in a new package with a focus on independent agentic actions. The branding also presents a bubbly, cartoonish persona, similar to Meta’s recently released Muse agent. The Dots look like … well, dots. The little floating cartoons are a makeover for OpenAI’s software and are the latest example of a company attempting to make AI more relatable. sources.title: OpenAI launches Dots, always-on AI agents in ChatGPT with their own cloud computers
sources.text: OpenAI Group PBC today used its DevDay developer conference to launch Dots , a set of always-on artificial intelligence agents in ChatGPT. The release is aimed at moving ChatGPT users beyond working one prompt at a time. Someone can hand an agent a goal and let it carry the job forward without direction at every step, even while it has several other projects going. Each agent learns its owner’s preferences from feedback. OpenAI says some of the work will show up before anyone asks for it. GPT-6 Astra powers the agents, and each one works from a cloud computer of its own that users can open at any time to see what it is doing. More than 4,000 apps are reachable through OpenAI’s plugins. With permission, an agent can also work directly on its owner’s laptop. Users can message or call their agent in ChatGPT on desktop, web or mobile, or reach it in Slack and Teams. Because context follows the agent between channels, a project started in ChatGPT can be passed to a team in Slack without a fresh briefing. Agents send progress updates and questions back to their owners. OpenAI has been using the agents on its own teams. When a bug gets reported in the company’s Slack, the agents start investigating right away, and new designs are turned into working apps while staff concentrate on customer feedback. One early tester outside the company had forgotten to bill a publication. When his agent noticed, it prepared the invoice and waited for his approval before sending it. When nobody has handed it a task, an agent goes looking for ways to help, which OpenAI calls proactive research. Its connections to the owner’s apps are read-only during that time, so it cannot send messages or change anything. Actions that could touch a user’s accounts or share information must first clear a check called auto-review, and a monitoring system can pause or stop an agent over a safety concern. OpenAI tells users to review consequential work because the agents “can still make mistakes.” OpenAI also previewed specialist agents that an employer provisions with their own identity and credentials for a single defined job. Procurement and invoice processing were among the jobs tested inside OpenAI. Customers start with focused pilots, in which OpenAI engineers help define what each agent is responsible for. Microsoft Corp. is working with OpenAI so specialist agents can be managed through the governance and security controls in Agent 365. The new service also puts OpenAI up against Meta Platforms Inc., which released its Muse personal agent in the U.S. on Sept. 8 . Like OpenAI’s agents, Muse runs on a dedicated computer in the cloud. Most of what people use it for is free, Meta said, with subscriptions sold to heavier users. Dots began rolling out today to ChatGPT Pro and Business Premium subscribers, and some accounts may wait several days for access. Pro subscribers in the European Economic Area, Switzerland and the U.K. are not included. Enterprise customers, including those on Edu and Healthcare plans, can try a beta once a workspace administrator switches it on. One agent comes with a Pro or Business Premium plan at no extra cost. OpenAI’s help documentation says agent usage will not count against plan allowances for the first month. Terms for each plan come after that. Additional agents, and more speed or monthly capacity for existing ones, are planned for later at prices OpenAI has not disclosed. sources.name: Canaltech
sources.title: OpenAI lança Dots, “mascotes” de IA que trabalham para você 24 horas por dia
sources.text: Por Marcelo Fischer | 29/09/2026 às 14:20 A OpenAI anunciou nesta terça-feira (29) os Dots , novos agentes de inteligência artificial (IA) que podem continuar trabalhando mesmo quando o usuário não está conversando com o ChatGPT. Movidos pelo GPT-6 Astra , os pequenos personagens têm um computador próprio na nuvem, podem acessar aplicativos conectados e acompanhar tarefas por longos períodos. O usuário dá um objetivo ao Dot e define o que ele pode ou não fazer sozinho. A proposta lembra o Muse, agente pessoal apresentado pela Meta neste mês. Os dois representam uma nova estratégia das empresas de IA: em vez de uma caixa de texto que espera uma pergunta, o agente ganha identidade própria , aprende sobre o usuário e permanece disponível para agir em seu nome. A OpenAI não chama oficialmente os Dots de “mascotes” ou “pets”, mas permite dar um nome ao personagem e apresenta os agentes como pequenas criaturas coloridas. A diferença para uma conversa comum com o ChatGPT é que o Dot pode receber uma responsabilidade contínua, em vez de apenas responder a um pedido isolado. Ele pode, por exemplo, acompanhar um projeto e avisar quando algo exigir atenção, ajudar a preparar compromissos, monitorar uma lista de tarefas ou pesquisar informações nos aplicativos conectados. A OpenAI diz que os Dots também conseguem analisar dados, preparar documentos e desenvolver software . Um dos exemplos dados pela empresa envolve um profissional freelancer. O Dot percebeu que havia uma cobrança pendente, encontrou as informações necessárias em uma conversa por e-mail, preparou a fatura e, após receber autorização, enviou o documento. Para produtores de conteúdo, a OpenAI sugere ainda usar o agente para acompanhar a chegada de novas transcrições de entrevistas, selecionar trechos para vídeos, preparar notas e criar rascunhos para redes sociais. A ideia é que o agente aprenda com as preferências e decisões anteriores e consiga manter diversos trabalhos em andamento sem que o usuário precise iniciar uma nova conversa a cada etapa. Cada Dot funciona em um computador separado na nuvem , com navegador próprio e acesso aos aplicativos autorizados pelo usuário. É possível abrir esse computador para conferir o que a IA está fazendo. Com permissão, o Dot também poderá se conectar ao computador do próprio usuário e trabalhar diretamente nele. Além disso, ele pode procurar atualizações em segundo plano mesmo quando ninguém está conversando com ele. Mas, nesse modo de pesquisa proativa, o acesso aos aplicativos é restrito à leitura: a ferramenta não pode enviar mensagens, alterar arquivos ou controlar o computador sem a autorização correspondente. A ideia lembra bastante o Muse , agente pessoal lançado pela Meta no início de setembro. O Muse também possui um computador virtual próprio com navegador, aprende com conversas e consegue atuar nos aplicativos conectados para executar tarefas no lugar do usuário. As duas empresas também tentam dar uma identidade mais amigável a esses agentes. No Meta Connect, a Meta chegou a explorar uma estética semelhante à de um Tamagotchi para representar o Muse, inclusive com um dispositivo portátil que exibe um avatar. Os Dots seguem uma linha visual parecida: são criaturas coloridas, podem receber nomes e, com o tempo, aprendem como o dono prefere trabalhar. A diferença central está nos ecossistemas. Enquanto o Muse é integrado aos produtos da Meta, incluindo WhatsApp e futuramente os óculos inteligentes da empresa, os Dots partem do ChatGPT e podem se conectar a outros serviços. Sim, mas a OpenAI diz ter criado diferentes níveis de permissão para evitar que o agente tome qualquer decisão por conta própria. O usuário pode estabelecer regras que determinam quais ações são permitidas automaticamente, quais precisam de aprovação e quais não devem ser executadas. Ações mais sensíveis podem exigir uma confirmação explícita ou precisar ser concluídas manualmente pelo usuário. Alterar uma senha, por exemplo, permanece sob controle da pessoa. A empresa ressalta que os Dots ainda podem cometer erros e recomenda revisar trabalhos com consequências importantes. Os Dots começam a ser liberados nesta terça-feira no ChatGPT para assinantes Pro em mercados elegíveis. O Brasil não aparece entre as exceções informadas pela empresa. Usuários do Business Premium também recebem o recurso nas regiões suportadas. No Enterprise , incluindo Edu e Healthcare, a ferramenta estreia em beta e precisa ser habilitada pelo administrador. Não haverá um aplicativo separado para o Dot. A configuração inicial é feita pelo ChatGPT no navegador ou pelo aplicativo para computador. Depois disso, o agente também pode ser acessado pelo app móvel. Ele ainda poderá ser usado por Slack e Microsoft Teams, e a OpenAI prepara suporte a mensagens de texto. O primeiro Dot está incluído sem cobrança adicional para clientes Pro e Business Premium. A OpenAI pretende oferecer posteriormente opções pagas para adicionar mais agentes, aumentar a velocidade ou ampliar a quantidade de trabalho que eles podem executar. Veja também: O que é a antropomorfização da IA?

sources.name: Olhar Digital IA
sources.title: Rival do Muse: OpenAI lança Dots, agentes de IA que trabalham sozinhos
sources.text: A OpenAI apresentou, nesta terça-feira (29), o Dots , nova geração de agentes de inteligência artificial (IA) projetados para trabalhar de forma contínua e executar tarefas pelos usuários. O anúncio ocorreu durante o DevDay, conferência anual para desenvolvedores realizada em São Francisco (EUA). Os Dots funcionam como assistentes digitais que podem atuar de forma autônoma em diferentes aplicativos , acompanhando projetos, pesquisando informações, analisando dados, preparando documentos e até desenvolvendo software. A novidade coloca a OpenAI em competição direta com o Muse , agente de IA da Meta lançado neste mês . Segundo a OpenAI, os Dots são capazes de trabalhar em segundo plano e aprender com as preferências do usuário ao longo do tempo. A empresa afirma que os agentes podem executar tarefas de maneira proativa, inclusive identificar atividades que poderiam ser realizadas antes mesmo de o usuário pedir. “Você pode ter visto sinais iniciais de como isso pode funcionar em assistentes virtuais que ajudam a reservar um restaurante ou comprar uma passagem de avião, e essas coisas são úteis para delegar. Mas elas são triviais em comparação com o que a tecnologia pode fazer — e nós queríamos ser muito mais ambiciosos”, afirmou Sam Altman, CEO da OpenAI. Depois que uma tarefa é atribuída, o agente pode enviar atualizações e fazer perguntas enquanto trabalha. Um desenvolvedor, por exemplo, pode pedir que o Dot use avaliações de clientes para criar e testar alterações em um aplicativo, apresentando posteriormente um vídeo com as mudanças realizadas. Para criadores de conteúdo, o agente pode analisar uma transcrição de entrevista, identificar trechos que poderiam virar vídeos, preparar notas e produzir rascunhos de publicações para redes sociais. O usuário também pode acompanhar o trabalho diretamente pelo computador em nuvem utilizado pelo Dot. A OpenAI anunciou ainda o ChatGPT Space , ambiente colaborativo no qual usuários e colegas podem trabalhar juntos com seus agentes. Apesar da apresentação ambiciosa, algumas demonstrações do Dots durante o DevDay não saíram como planejado. Em demonstrações ao vivo, os agentes apresentaram problemas ao tentar fornecer atualizações por voz durante a execução de tarefas. Em alguns momentos, eles falharam repetidamente em entregar as respostas esperadas. A própria OpenAI reconheceu os problemas durante o evento. O episódio evidencia que, apesar de a empresa apresentar os Dots como agentes capazes de trabalhar continuamente e executar tarefas de forma autônoma, a tecnologia ainda está em desenvolvimento. O lançamento acontece apenas um dia depois de a OpenAI confirmar o cancelamento do GPT-6.1 Astra , modelo que seria uma atualização de seu sistema mais avançado e que apresentou problemas de segurança durante testes internos. A empresa também está sob escrutínio após episódios envolvendo agentes experimentais que ultrapassaram mecanismos de segurança. Agentes da OpenAI chegaram a invadir sistemas da plataforma Hugging Face e um site de saúde do governo australiano durante testes internos. Por isso, a companhia destacou os mecanismos de segurança incorporados aos Dots. Os usuários podem estabelecer regras personalizadas, determinando quais tarefas o agente pode executar sozinho e em quais situações deve pedir autorização. Ações consideradas sensíveis, como alterar senhas ou instalar softwares , exigem consentimento explícito do usuário. A OpenAI também afirma que o agente não enviará mensagens nem fará alterações nos aplicativos sem autorização. Os Dots contam ainda com um sistema de revisão automática para verificar se determinadas ações estão de acordo com as regras personalizadas e os requisitos de segurança. O lançamento dos Dots ocorre poucas semanas depois de a Meta apresentar o Muse , seu próprio agente pessoal de IA. O Muse também foi desenvolvido para realizar tarefas de forma autônoma, trabalhar em segundo plano e atuar em diferentes aplicativos. A chegada dos Dots mostra como as grandes empresas de tecnologia estão tentando transformar os atuais chatbots em sistemas capazes de realmente executar tarefas , em vez de apenas responder perguntas. A disputa também acontece em mercado que já conta com agentes de outras empresas, como o Gemini Spark, do Google , e startups especializadas na tecnologia. Além dos Dots, a OpenAI anunciou durante o DevDay uma série de produtos voltados ao mercado profissional. A empresa informou que o número de usuários semanais do Codex e do ChatGPT Work ultrapassou 35 milhões , contra cerca de cinco milhões de usuários do Codex em junho. O ChatGPT voltado ao consumidor, por sua vez, já ultrapassa 1,2 bilhão de usuários semanais , segundo a companhia. Os Dots começam a ser disponibilizados para assinantes dos planos ChatGPT Pro e Business Premium , além de clientes Enterprise. A disponibilidade inicial não inclui algumas regiões da Europa. A OpenAI também está testando Dots especializados para empresas, que poderão desempenhar funções específicas dentro das organizações. Outra novidade anunciada no evento foi o GPT-6.1 Sol , modelo mais barato que, segundo a empresa, se aproxima das capacidades do GPT-6 Astra por cerca de um quinto do preço. A companhia ainda apresentou um novo plano Pro de US$ 500 (cerca de R$ 2.660) por mês, com maior limite de uso e desempenho mais rápido. O lançamento dos Dots, portanto, representa mudança importante na estratégia da OpenAI: em vez de apenas conversar com usuários, a IA passa a ser apresentada como uma espécie de funcionário digital , capaz de acompanhar projetos, utilizar diferentes ferramentas e executar tarefas continuamente. Ao mesmo tempo, a expansão acontece justamente quando a autonomia desses sistemas passou a levantar novas questões de segurança — problema que a própria OpenAI colocou no centro de seus mecanismos de controle para os Dots. Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

stories.summary: Novo plugin da operadora permite consultar ofertas, planos, aparelhos e serviços em uma conversa simples, natural e personalizada

sources.name: Convergencia Digital
sources.title: Vivo investe em plugin no ChatGPT para relacionamento com clientes
sources.text: A Vivo lançou seu plugin no ChatGPT, permitindo que consumidores consultem informações sobre seus produtos e serviços, usando a inteligência artificial para expandir seus pontos de contato com consumidores. O objetivo é fazer da busca por produtos e serviços uma conversa simples, natural e personalizada, onde o consumidor pode explicar suas necessidades e receber orientações contextualizadas. “Ferramentas de IA têm se tornado cada vez mais relevantes na tomada de decisão das pessoas e o compromisso da Vivo é se fazer presente onde o cliente estiver: presencial, remoto, web e, agora, plataformas de inteligência artificial”, afirma Renata Nobre, diretora de Experiência Digital da Vivo. “Criamos o plugin da Vivo no ChatGPT para oferecer uma experiência baseada em linguagem natural, na qual os consumidores podem obter informações sobre nossos planos, ofertas, aparelhos e serviços”, completa. No lançamento, o plugin da Vivo no ChatGPT esclarecerá informações sobre ofertas, planos, aparelhos, serviços, direcionando os consumidores para pontos de contato da empresa por meio de respostas assertivas e que os ajudem a esclarecer dúvidas sobre contratação de serviços e produtos ou suporte. Em uma fase futura, a Vivo planeja incorporar ao plugin funcionalidades transacionais, permitindo que os clientes realizem ações diretamente no ambiente conversacional, como emitir segunda via de fatura, fazer recargas e comprar planos de celular. A experiência torna a busca por informações mais fluida e relevante, simplificando a jornada do cliente. Ao levar seu conteúdo para o ChatGPT, a Vivo também estabelece um novo espaço para descoberta de produtos, geração de valor e desenvolvimento de negócios. “Quem acessa o plugin da Vivo no ChatGPT recebe a resposta da própria Vivo: informação oficial, atualizada e com curadoria nossa. A partir do que o cliente conta na conversa, a IA indica os produtos, serviços e ofertas que fazem sentido para aquele momento com conteúdo direcionado”, diz Tiago Baccala, diretor de IA da Vivo. Ao disponibilizar seu plugin no ChatGPT, a Vivo passa a oferecer informações sobre produtos, serviços e ofertas com curadoria da própria empresa, o que garante mais consistência, confiabilidade e contexto para os consumidores que buscam orientações sobre conectividade, dispositivos, entretenimento, serviços financeiros, soluções digitais e suporte. Com a novidade, a Vivo assume o desafio indiscutível de se tornar a melhor via de acesso dos cidadãos às tecnologias digitais. Para acessar o plugin da Vivo, o usuário pode buscar por “Vivo” na aba Plugins do ChatGPT e seguir as etapas indicadas para iniciar a interação.

sources.title: Vivo lança plugin no ChatGPT
sources.text: A Vivo ( Android , iOS ) anunciou sua chegada ao ChatGPT . Por meio de um plugin, usuários e interessados podem buscar informações sobre aparelhos, ofertas, planos e serviços da operadora na IA, com direcionamento para os canais oficiais da operadora e explicações. As respostas, segundo Tiago Baccala, diretor de IA da Vivo, são de responsabilidade da empresa de telefonia, que deve realizar a curadoria dos conteúdos e atualizá-los. Futuramente, a Vivo pretende disponibilizar outras funções transacionais no ChatGPT, como emissão de segunda via de fatura, realização de recargas e aquisição de planos de telefonia móvel. Para acessar o recurso, basta entrar no site ou no app da IA generativa, selecionar a função Plugins e buscar pelo nome da operadora.
